question: After repairing OTLP/HTTP routing, should OpenClaw core establish a persistent exporter and shared instrumentation API with this proposed data, transport, and lifecycle contract?
rationale: The protocol defect has a mechanical repair, but deciding what future data may be exported, whether plaintext remote endpoints are acceptable, and whether the telemetry names and helpers become stable core API requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a bounded core contract
options.body: Land after fixing HTTP routing, enforcing documented non-sensitive fields and transport guidance, and adding current-head UI and collector proof.

options.title: Keep it probe-only and internal
options.body: Internalize the instrumentation helpers and dispose exporters after the diagnostic probe so the feature does not establish a general telemetry surface.

options.title: Pause observability groundwork
options.body: Defer the PR until a maintainer-sponsored design defines long-term telemetry ownership and privacy policy.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Land after fixing HTTP routing, enforcing documented non-sensitive fields and transport guidance, and adding current-head UI and collector proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent merged ownership across the exact cross-cutting tray, diagnostics, settings, localization, and test surfaces.
